finding: Share of handpumps non-functional at any time in sub-Saharan Africa
value: about 25 (one in four; extrapolated 26; bounds 22-29); older RWSN estimate 36
citation: Foster T., Furey S., Banks B. & Willetts J. (2019) Functionality of handpump water supplies: a review of data from sub-Saharan Africa and the Asia-Pacific region. International Journal of Water Resources Development, doi 10.1080/07900627.2018.1543117 (online 11 Mar 2019); RWSN (2009)
notes: Confirmed: 'approximately one in four handpumps in sub-Saharan Africa are non-functional at any point in time, which in 2015 was roughly equivalent to 175,000 inoperative water points'; extrapolation gives about 680,000 handpumps in SSA in 2015 of which 175,000 (26%) non-functional; country-level medians 27-28%, means 29-31%, interquartile range 20-34%; allowing 1 point per year drift gives 22-29%. RWSN (2009): 36% from expert estimates for 20 countries, range 10-65%. Review covers 47 countries (38 SSA, 9 Asia-Pacific). Original note corrected: 175,000 is the number NON-FUNCTIONAL, not the total stock. 'Cameroon 2024: one in three' is not in this source and remains unverified.
